_doc: Stream E (play-test 2, Q9/Q11/Q16/Q20). What every trader in Torbor Downs sells, and for how much. Stream A runs the shops (buy, sell, buyback, restock), stream D-UI draws the window (tabs = `categories`, then `goods`), stream D-world draws the shopfront from the shop's `sign` (data/provinces/offices.json says WHICH plot each trader works in). A shop is `kinds.<kind>`; a town lists the kinds it has in `towns.<town>.shops` (every hub town of the province is listed). GEAR (`categories`): rolled from emberveil items.json bases with Farhold's loot generator at the BUYER's level (min 1, never above the town's `levelCap`), `count` items per category, `rarity` weights; rolled once per restock per shop (the same stock for everyone in that town copy), restocked every `pricing.restockMinutes`. GOODS (`goods`): fixed items always in stock — `id` = an items.json `potions` key (`source: 'potion'`), a Farhold js/gear.js GEAR_BASES key (`source: 'gear'`: mounts, lights, quivers) or a Thousandvale good (`source: 'good'`, described in `goodsCatalog` here); `price` = gold, `minLevel` = the level a character must be to buy it. PRICES: gear = Loot.price (items.json basePrice 15 x priceQualityMult x priceRarityMult) x (1 + `pricing.perItemLevel` x (item level - 1)) x the town's `priceMult`; a GEAR_BASES item with its own `basePrice` keeps that (Farhold rpg.price). Selling gives `pricing.sellFactor` of the price; the last `pricing.buyback` items you sold come back at what you were paid. Scale check: a kill pays 3 + level gold (js/sim/quests.js KILL_GOLD), so a level-2 healing potion (9 g) is about two kills, the first horse (60 g) about a dozen kills plus the starting chain's purses (the chain pays ~550 g by level 5). SERVICES: the barber (Q20) and the stable master's stabling are `services`.

pricing.note: No repair bills (PLAN §13). Buyback is per character and kept until the next restock.

travel_rations.name: Travel rations
travel_rations.desc: Bread, cheese and something that was once a sausage. Eat out of combat to recover health over 20 seconds.

trail_ale.name: Mug of trail ale
trail_ale.desc: Drink out of combat to recover mana over 20 seconds. Tastes of the barrel.

hearty_stew.name: Bowl of hearty stew
hearty_stew.desc: Eat out of combat: recover health and mana over 20 seconds, then +5% health for 30 minutes.

torch_bundle.name: Bundle of torches
torch_bundle.desc: Six pitch torches. One lit torch lights a dark room or cave for ten minutes.

recall_charm.name: Recall charm
recall_charm.desc: Snap it to walk out of the wilds to your bound inn after 5 seconds of standing still. One use.

whetstone.name: Whetstone
whetstone.desc: Sharpen an edge before a fight: +3% weapon damage for 15 minutes.

armour_oil.name: Armour oil
armour_oil.desc: Oil the joints: +4% armour for 15 minutes.

silver_dust.name: Pinch of silver dust
silver_dust.desc: Rub it on your weapon: +6% damage to the dead and the cursed for 10 minutes.

fletching_kit.name: Fletching kit
fletching_kit.desc: Fresh flights and heads for a bow or crossbow: +4% ranged damage for 15 minutes. (There is no ammunition; this is just better arrows.)

herb_poultice.name: Herb poultice
herb_poultice.desc: Press it on a wound: stops bleeding and heals a little at once.

dye_pot.name: Pot of cloth dye
dye_pot.desc: Recolour one piece of cloth or leather you are wearing (pick the colour in the window).

saddle_bags.name: Saddle bags
saddle_bags.desc: Twelve more bag slots while you own a mount. Kept on the mount.

oat_sack.name: Sack of oats
oat_sack.desc: Feed your mount: +10% riding speed for 30 minutes.

lucky_horseshoe.name: Lucky horseshoe
lucky_horseshoe.desc: Nail it over your door, or hang it from your saddle. Does nothing measurable. People swear by it.

general.name: General Goods
says: Fair prices! Fairish prices!
If I don't have it, you don't need it. Probably.
Potions on the left, regrets on the right.

market.name: Market Stall
says: Everything's been owned before. That's how you know it works.
Haggle? I love to haggle. I always win.
Fresh off a cart. Which cart? Don't ask.

weaponsmith.name: Smithy
says: Mind the sparks.
Good steel doesn't care who swings it.
Bring it here, I'll take the dent out. Free. Don't tell anyone.

armourer.name: Armourer
says: Try it on. No, the other way round.
A good coat of mail is a hug that saves your life.
Plate's heavy. So is a grave.

bowyer.name: Bowyer & Fletcher
says: Straight shafts, true flights, no refunds.
A bow is a stick that's angry at a string.
No, I don't sell arrows. Nobody counts arrows round here.

apothecary.name: Apothecary
says: Don't lick that. Don't lick ANY of it.
Willow bark for the head, nettle for the joints, and this one for your enemies.
Everything here's a cure for something. Possibly you.

tailor.name: Tailor
says: Stand still. STILL. Breathe in.
Robes are armour for people who'd rather not be hit at all.
That tear? Cost you extra. That bloodstain? Free.

jeweller.name: Jeweller
says: Every ring has a story. Most of them end with a fight.
Gold doesn't tarnish. People do.
Two rings, two hands, no limits. Well — two limits.

stable.name: Stables

goods.note: the owner wants to try a mount (play-test 2, Q16): the plain horse is sold from level 1, ahead of PLAN §6.5's mount-at-10 ladder

stable.label: Swap your riding mount (mounts you own are kept here)

says: Mind his back legs. And his front ones. And his teeth.
Every horse here's been ridden by someone braver than you. Don't worry, they're fine. Mostly.
Oats, water, a kind word. Same as people, really.

inn.name: Inn

bind.label: Make this inn your home (recall and respawn here)

says: Stew's on. It's always on.
Rooms upstairs, rats downstairs, everyone's happy.

provisioner.name: Provisioner
says: Rations, rope, a torch and a lucky horseshoe. Everything a hero forgets.
Pack light. Pack bread. Pack more bread.
Going far? Buy two.

barber.name: Barber

appearance.label: Change your look
appearance.editor: the character editor (the same one the title screen's Customize Appearance opens), limited to what this barber does
appearance.note: price = list price x (1 + perLevel x (level - 1)), rounded; the first change a character ever makes here is free. Class outfits are not the barber's (gear is gear).

says: Sit. A little off the top? A little off the side? A little off the ear?
I've cut the hair of three kings. Well. Three men who said they were kings.
New face, new you. Same debts, mind.

broker.name: Hiring Hall
says: Blades for hire, priced by the day, buried at your expense.
Need a shield arm? I've got six. Attached to people, mostly.

unbinder.name: Unbinder

retrain.label: Take back a talent or a perk

says: What was learned can be unlearned. For a fee.
Regret is a door. I have the key. It's gold-plated.

healer.name: Bonesetter
says: Sit. No, not there, that's where I keep the leeches.
Whatever it is, I've seen worse. Yesterday, mostly.

Torborhold.note: the starting town: every trader the owner asked for (Q9)

Orrinsford.note: pilgrims' town: maces and silver for the dead

Copperdell.note: mining city: hammers and picks cheap, jewellery better

Halsbridge.note: the province capital: everything, and dearer

Hermit's Rest.note: forest city: the best bows, no plate

Brackwater.note: fen town: cheap antidotes, no stables in a bog

Last Lantern.note: the last town before the Scar: dear, and short of everything but potions

Pail and Plough.note: the crossroads inn on the south road (a set piece, not a town): Marra feeds you

goods.note: the owner wants to try a mount (play-test 2, Q16): the plain horse is sold from level 1, ahead of PLAN §6.5's mount-at-10 ladder

stable.label: Swap your riding mount (mounts you own are kept here)

bind.label: Make this inn your home (recall and respawn here)

_rolesDoc: MADE by tools/content-shops.mjs from `kinds` (do not edit by hand): stream A's js/sim/shops.js reads roles.<role> = { title, sells: [{ base, rarity }], markup } (+ goods, services, mounts, sign, light, kind). `cat` = the shop tab (the kind's category label).
